_doc: The realm's past (sim/realm-bake). Before day 1, every district lives `dawns` days (0 to maxDawns, chosen at New game) on an abstract day: food by season, land and weather; despair pulled toward the wound it carries (which itself rises and falls on a slow tide: tide.local per district, tide.realm for all of them, periods in years) and eased or deepened by its hearths (glow); neighbours feud, pact and go to war by the same meters as civic/district-relations; and rare events befall it (events). Each district keeps the greatest and the latest of what happened to it (keepGreat / keepRecent), which its people retell (tell), and the realm's time is cut into named ages (ages). Units are per dawn unless named otherwise. Nothing here is rolled in play: the bake is a pure function of (seed, dawns).

presets.label: A young world
presets.hint: No past but the one its people were born with. The world as it has always started.

presets.label: A generation
presets.hint: 25 years: one war, one bad winter, one name people still say.

presets.label: A century
presets.hint: 100 years of pacts, plagues and harvests behind every district.

presets.label: An age
presets.hint: 1,000 years. Lands have fallen to ash and been rekindled more than once.

presets.label: Deep time
presets.hint: 3,571 years: the oldest world there is.

summaries: {ago}, {district} went to war with {other}. They call it the War of the {war} now. Our side held the field, for what that bought.
{ago} the levies marched on {other}. The War of the {war}: we won it, and buried a good many winning it.
codas: Winning is a kind of losing too.
The banners are still up in the hall, moth-eaten.

summaries: {ago}, {other} came over the border. The War of the {war}. We lost it, and paid for the losing.
{ago} {district} fought {other} and was beaten. The War of the {war}: half the old families date their grief from it.
codas: Nobody here forgave {other}. Not really.
You can still see where the wall was.

summaries: {ago}, the seats of {district} and {other} put their seals to a pact. The carts ran both ways after that.
{ago} we swore a trade pact with {other}. For a while the roads were worth walking.
codas: A pact is only as warm as the hands that hold it.
Good years, those.

summaries: {ago}, the grey cough went through {town}. It took one in ten, and the rest stopped looking each other in the eye.
{ago} a sickness came to {town} with the carts. They burned the bedding in the square for a month.
codas: That is when the doors started being shut at night.
Some houses never opened again.

summaries: {ago}, {town} burned. Half the roofs in a night. They built it back lower and meaner.
{ago} a fire took the old quarter of {town}. People stood and watched, which is the part nobody talks about.
codas: The stones by the well are still black.
Fire we could have fought, if anyone had cared to.

summaries: {ago}, the water came up over {town} and stayed a month. The stores rotted where they stood.
{ago} the river took the low fields by {town}. We ate thin for a year after.
codas: The mark is still on the chapel door.
Water forgets. People don't.

summaries: {ago}, the frost came early and would not leave. {district} ate its seed grain that winter.
{ago} was the winter of the long frost. In {town} they burned the fences to keep the old ones alive.
codas: Nobody plants late any more.
We counted the living in spring.

summaries: {ago}, the blight came through the fields of {district}. The whole harvest went black in a week.
{ago} the crop failed around {town}. Not thin: failed. There was nothing to bring in.
codas: That is the year the young ones started leaving.
You never trust a field again, after.

summaries: {ago}, the stores of {district} ran out before the spring did. People remember who shared and who did not.
{ago} was the hungry season. In {town} they boiled harness leather.
codas: Hunger keeps a ledger.
Some families are still not spoken to.

summaries: {ago}, {district} had a harvest the old folk still measure the others by. Carts stood loaded in the lanes.
{ago} the fields by {town} gave double. There was dancing, they say. Real dancing.
codas: We could have that again.
Hard to believe now, I know.

summaries: {ago}, a stranger called {name} walked into {town} carrying something like an ember. Hearths that had been cold for years were lit by the time they left.
{ago} one of the spark-carriers came through {town}. {name}, the name was. People woke up. That is the only way I can put it.
codas: Then they walked on, and it was ours to keep. We did not keep all of it.
You have the same look about you, if you don't mind my saying.

summaries: {ago}, the creed of {district} split down the middle over a matter nobody can now explain. {town} still has two meeting halls.
{ago} half the seat walked out on the other half. Neighbours were shouted at over it, and {other} never forgot.
codas: Being right kept nobody warm.
It was never really about the creed.

summaries: {ago}, a third of the young families of {district} packed their carts and went to {other}. The houses are still empty.
{ago} people simply started leaving {town}. No quarrel, no farewell. Just fewer chimneys smoking each week.
codas: You can't blame them. I tried.
Some sent letters. Then the letters stopped.

summaries: {ago}, {town} held its first great fair. Traders came from {other} and further. For a week the place remembered itself.
{ago} the market at {town} was the talk of the realm. People met their wives and husbands at that fair.
codas: We should hold one again.
The fair field is pasture now.

summaries: {ago}, a star with a tail hung over {district} for nine nights. Everybody had an opinion about what it meant.
{ago} the hairy star came. The creed said one thing, the old women said another.
codas: Whatever it meant, it meant it quietly.
Nothing happened after. That was the strange part.

summaries: {ago}, a bandit called {name} held the roads of {district} for three seasons. Carts went armed or not at all.
{ago} {name} and a band of broken men took a toll on every road out of {town}.
codas: Some say {name} was one of ours, once.
The roads were never quite trusted again.

summaries: {ago}, when the old seat-holder died, two claimed the chair. {name} took it in the end, and {district} was a long time healing.
{ago} was the year of two seats. {name} won it; the other side's children still sit at the back.
codas: Ask in {town} which side their family was on. Go on.
A chair. All that over a chair.

summaries: {ago}, the last lit hearth in {district} went out. Nobody marked the day. They only noticed, later, that it had been a while.
{ago} {district} fell to ash. Not in a night: one cold house at a time, until there was no one left to mind.
codas: That is the worst of it: it was quiet.
We are what was left over.

summaries: {ago}, {district} came back from the ash. One hearth, then a street of them, then the seat itself.
{ago} the fires were lit again in {town}. People who had not spoken in years stood in the lane and wept.
codas: So it can be done. Remember that.
It only took one to start it.

summaries: {ago}, {district} was the brightest land in the realm. Travellers could see {town} from a day off, they say, all its windows lit.
{ago} every hearth in {town} was burning. People walked here from {other} just to sit in it.
codas: We were proud. Maybe too proud.
I'd give a good deal to see it once.

summaries: {ago}, the bright years of {district} ended. Nothing took them. We just stopped tending what we had.
{ago} {town} began to go dark at the edges. By the time anyone said it aloud it was half gone.
codas: A fire is a thing you do, not a thing you have.
Nobody thinks it will be their house.
